passage: The ice-cream cart rang its bell at the gate of Sunrise Colony, and a dozen kids ran for it. Imran was first in line when Usha squeezed in front, her elbow knocking his arm. "Hey! You're so rude," he shouted. "Always pushing." Usha pointed at her building. "Mummy's calling me for dinner, I only have one minute!" Imran didn't hear that part. The next evening Imran was the one running late for his tabla class. He shoved past two kids at the cart, grabbed his cone and ran. "Sorry, sorry, I'm late!" he called over his shoulder, feeling perfectly reasonable. That night he told his father, "Usha pushes because she's rude. I only pushed because I had tabla." His father looked at him for a long moment.

qa.q: Why was Imran in a hurry the next evening?
qa.a: Imran was running late for his tabla class.

qa.q: Why did Imran feel perfectly reasonable shoving past the kids?
qa.a: Imran felt comfortable with his own push because he knew all about his late tabla class, while Usha's reason never reached him.

qa.q: What could Imran's father ask to help him?
qa.a: His father could ask, 'What did Usha say when she pushed?' so Imran remembers that her mummy was calling her too.

qa.q: How might the two kids Imran shoved see him?
qa.a: They only saw a boy pushing past them, so they might call him rude, just as Imran called Usha.

grounding: A boy excuses his own push by his hurry but calls a girl's push rude, ignoring that she was in a hurry too.

passage:
"You pushed me off the swing!" Noor said, brushing sand off her knees.
"I didn't push. I just needed a turn fast. The bell was about to ring," said Thomas.
"So? Yesterday when Kiran pushed you off the slide, you said he was a bully."
"Because he is. He pushes everyone."
"And you pushed me."
"That's different. I had a reason."
"Maybe Kiran had a reason too."
"Like what?"
Noor shrugged. "Maybe the bell was about to ring for him too."
Thomas kicked at the sand. "His reason is he's mean."
"And your reason is the bell?"
"Yes."
Noor climbed back onto the swing. "Then I'm keeping it, because the bell hasn't rung."

qa.q: Why does Thomas say Noor was pushed off the swing?
qa.a: Thomas says the push was only about needing a turn fast because the bell was about to ring.

qa.q: Why does Thomas think that push is different from Kiran's?
qa.a: Thomas feels that rush from inside, so that push has a reason, while Kiran is only seen from outside, so Kiran's push gets called mean.

qa.q: What could Thomas try when he wants to call someone a bully?
qa.a: Thomas could ask what reason Kiran might have had, just as Thomas had one.

qa.q: How does Noor see the two pushes?
qa.a: Noor sees them as the same kind of push and wonders why only Thomas gets to have a reason.

grounding: A child says their own push came from being rushed but a classmate's push came from being mean.

passage: I'm Ronak, and this happened in the morning assembly line. Shreya pushed me from behind and I nearly fell on the boy in front. I told Manjula Miss, "Shreya is rude. She always pushes." Then, when the line moved to our classroom, I pushed Deepu so I could get the window seat before anyone else. Manjula Miss said, "Good boys don't push, Ronak." I said I was in a hurry because my bag was so heavy. Later I found out Shreya had been pushed by the big boys behind her. I felt a bit silly. My push had a reason, but I never asked about hers. Now I think maybe she had a reason too.

qa.q: Why did Ronak push Deepu?
qa.a: He pushed Deepu so he could get the window seat before anyone else.

qa.q: How did Ronak feel after learning why Shreya pushed?
qa.a: He felt a bit silly, because his own push had a reason but he never asked about hers.

qa.q: What would you advise Ronak when someone pushes him in the line?
qa.a: Before calling them rude, he could look behind them or ask what happened, since someone might be pushing them too.

qa.q: How might Deepu feel about being pushed for the window seat?
qa.a: Deepu might think Ronak is rude, just as Ronak thought about Shreya, because Deepu can't see the heavy bag.

grounding: A boy blames a classmate's rudeness for her push while excusing his own push by his hurry.

passage:
Class teacher's note, Seema, Class 3B, Monday.
In the lunch rush today, Jomon pushed Deepak aside to reach the tap. Deepak scraped his elbow on the wall. When I asked Jomon what happened, he said quickly, "I had to push, Miss, the bell was ringing and I was so thirsty."
Later, in class, he complained, "Deepak pushed me in the morning line! He's so rude. He always does rude things."
I asked him whether Deepak might have been in a hurry too. "No, he's just rude."
What I did next: I sat both boys together after lunch, asked each to tell me why they pushed. Both said, "I was in a hurry." Jomon looked at Deepak with his mouth open. I have moved the tap queue earlier so it isn't a rush.

qa.q: What did Deepak scrape when he fell against the wall?
qa.a: Deepak scraped his elbow.

qa.q: Why did Jomon feel his own push was fine but Deepak's push was rude?
qa.a: Jomon was annoyed at Deepak but felt his own push had a reason, because he could feel his own hurry and thirst but not Deepak's, so Deepak's push seemed to come from being a rude person.

qa.q: What did Seema do after lunch, and what did Jomon discover?
qa.a: She sat both boys together and asked why each had pushed, and Jomon heard Deepak give the same reason, being in a hurry, which surprised him.

qa.q: How might Deepak have felt about being called rude by Jomon?
qa.a: Deepak probably felt it was unfair, since he had also just been rushing, and he had been the one who got hurt at the tap.

grounding: A teacher's note shows a boy explaining his own push by a hurry while calling another child's push rude.

passage:
Thursday
Today in the school bus line Ojas pushed me so hard my bag fell in a puddle. Ojas is SO rude. He always pushes. He never says sorry. I don't like him at all.
Then in the evening, at the park, the ice cream man was leaving and I ran and I pushed a small girl out of the way. She cried a little bit. But that was not my fault, the ice cream man was going and I had to be fast. Anyone would push.
Mummy asked if Ojas was maybe rushing for the bus. I said no, because he is just like that. Then Mummy said, "And you were just like that at the park, my boy?" and I said NO, because I had a reason.
I don't think Mummy understands. Also my ice cream was mango.
Harish

qa.q: Where did Harish's bag fall when Ojas pushed him?
qa.a: His bag fell in a puddle.

qa.q: Why does Harish feel his own push at the park was not his fault?
qa.a: Harish felt annoyed at Ojas but saw his own push as fair, since he knew he was rushing for the ice cream man, while Ojas's push seemed to show that Ojas is a rude person.

qa.q: What question could Mummy ask next to help Harish see both pushes more evenly?
qa.a: She could ask what Ojas might have been rushing for, the way Harish rushed for the ice cream, so Harish works out on his own that both had reasons.

qa.q: How might the small girl at the park see Harish's push?
qa.a: To the small girl it probably felt just as rude as Ojas's push felt to Harish, since she only saw a big kid shove her and did not know about the ice cream man leaving.

grounding: A boy's diary shows him explaining his own push by hurry while calling another boy's push a sign of being rude.
